intro: The marketing for Target Company Research promises automation, accuracy and speed. Its own pages also carry placeholders, conflicting lists and claims no third party verifies. This review keeps the pitch and the paperwork separate.
The platform is browser-only, with no app to install. Signals arrive from the models, trades execute through a broker partner, and the US$250 minimum opens access to 11 assets and the demo.
Our method is a desk review: no funded account, no trades. We read the published material in full, including unfilled placeholders and contradictions, and scored five fixed dimensions.
whatItClaims: Around-the-clock support through the partner desk.
Signals generated without manual chart reading.
A US$250 minimum deposit to start.
Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
whatWeChecked: The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.
The withdrawal path: steps and any fees the page omits.
The ownership trail: who operates the platform and where.
The support channels: live chat, email or phone availability.

redFlags: A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.
The demo promised in the pitch but buried in the flow.

faqs.q: Is it really fee-free?
faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

faqs.q: What is the minimum deposit?
faqs.a: US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

faqs.q: Is Target Company Research safe, legit or a scam?
faqs.a: We found no scam indicators in the product, which reads as a functioning AI trading service. The conditions are editorial: claims without verification, conflicting figures and restriction lists that disagree. We rate it safe to research with the conditions in this review.

faqs.q: How fast are withdrawals?
faqs.a: The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
4.8 is our number, and it means the product works with conditions attached. The demo costs nothing; use it while the claims remain unproven.
